title: Exact free module resolution of the augmentation on a total simplicial site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_p$ ($p\ge0$) and $\mathcal D$ be small sites in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For each order-preserving map $\alpha:[p]\to[q]$ in the simplex category [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], let $u_\alpha:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_q)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_p)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Suppose their identity and composition identifications satisfy the cocycle laws, and let $a_p:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_p)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ have compatible coherent identifications $a_pu_\alpha\simeq a_q$. A total module is a family $F_p$ with transition maps $u_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_q$ compatible with these identifications. Fix a commutative ring $\Lambda$, use modules over its constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and use the canonical constant-coefficient inverse images. For a $\Lambda_{\mathcal D}$-module $G$, let $a^{-1}G$ be the total module with components $a_m^{-1}G$ and the augmentation identifications as transitions. Define $P_p(G)$ by
$$P_p(G)_m=\bigoplus_{\alpha:[p]\to[m]}a_m^{-1}G.$$
Its transition for $\beta:[m]\to[k]$ sends the $\alpha$ summand to the $\beta\alpha$ summand through $u_\beta^{-1}a_m^{-1}G\cong a_k^{-1}G$. For $p\ge1$ let $d_i:P_p(G)\to P_{p-1}(G)$ send the $\alpha$ summand in component $m$ identically to the $\alpha\delta_i$ summand, where $\delta_i:[p-1]\to[p]$ omits $i$. Let $\epsilon:P_0(G)\to a^{-1}G$ be the fold map in every component. These are morphisms of total modules, and the augmented chain complex with boundary $\sum_{i=0}^p(-1)^id_i$,
$$\cdots\longrightarrow P_2(G)\longrightarrow P_1(G)\longrightarrow P_0(G)\xrightarrow{\epsilon}a^{-1}G\longrightarrow0,$$
is exact. For every total module $I$, restriction of a morphism $P_p(G)\to I$ to the identity-labelled summand in component $p$ is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Tot}}(P_p(G),I)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_{\mathcal C_p}}(a_p^{-1}G,I_p).$$
Its inverse sends $f:a_p^{-1}G\to I_p$ on the $\alpha$ summand of component $m$ to $I(\alpha)\circ u_\alpha^{-1}f$, using $a_m^{-1}G\cong u_\alpha^{-1}a_p^{-1}G$. In particular $\epsilon$ corresponds to the identity when $I=a^{-1}G$.
